transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-06
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Marta Gomez (Redwood SE, sat in); Alex Morgan (Head of ML, Lumen); Jia Chen (Platform Eng); Daniel Ruiz (SRE)

Summary:
- Walkthrough of Redwood model catalog UI + API paths for picking open models, reading benchmark rows, and exporting compatibility matrix CSVs.
- Discussed benchmark methodology, TCO knobs (batching, quantization, routing), and private deployment options (VPC + KMS).
- Agreed POC: run a 2-week bench comparing 3 open models with Lumen's queries on Redwood Dedicated and Hosted endpoints.
- Action owners assigned and security docs to be shared.

Topics covered:
- Catalog filters, tags, and pinned model versions
- Bench matrix interpretation and custom metric columns
- Kernel/quantization compatibility notes and hardware mapping
- Networking / VPC / KMS / audit logs for Private deployment
- Rollout strategy: canary routing + automatic fallback to cheaper variant

Action items (short):
- See metadata for owners/due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Priya: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, um we've got about an hour, we'll run through the catalog UI first then the bench matrix and then leave time for the infra questions and next steps. Alex — thanks for making time.
[00:12] Alex: yeah thanks, excited to see how you handle open models. we've got a tight budget so cost is a blocker.
[00:18] Priya: totally, we built the Optimize controls to help with exactly that — show cost vs latency tradeoffs. Samir will drive the bench piece.
[00:25] Samir: hey hi, yeah quick note, my name is Samir Patel, I'm the SE on inference runtime, I'll show the kernel and quant notes after the UI walk. apologies if i stumble on the demo environment, network's a bit flaky today.
[00:38] Jia: no worries. quick context — we run a mixture of real-time customer support prompts (p95 target 120ms) and nightly embeddings generation, and the latter can be batched. also we have an on-prem box for regulated accounts.
[00:52] Priya: perfect that's useful. so walk-through — catalog page, top-left filter, you can pick 'open models' then choose a prune level, quantized variants are visible as sibling rows. notice the bench column on the right which shows median latency and tokens/sec from Redwood-verified runs — but those are from our lab hardware, so we'll run a customer bench to align.
[01:20] Alex: can you show how to compare two models side by side? like Mistral-ish vs other?
[01:24] Priya: sure — select two checkboxes, hit 'compare' — you get a diff view with quality metrics, bench metrics, and a compatibility matrix export link. the compatibility matrix contains supported kernels, quantization flags, and estimated cost per 1k tokens on both Hosted and Dedicated.
[01:45] Daniel: the compatibility matrix — does it include KV cache behavior? we have long-context chat sessions and cache behaviour affects latency a lot.
[01:52] Samir: yes, we annotate per-model KV cache warm start times, including an estimated p95 for cache misses and hits. slight note — the transcript system shows 'K V cash' sometimes in our logs — sorry, uh, the auto-transcript's noisy.
[02:06] Alex: haha noted. could you explain the bench methodology briefly? we want reproducible numbers.
[02:10] Samir: sure — bench is a mix of synthetic and replay. we run a replay harness for customer queries to capture realistic seq lengths; synthetic runs vary sequence and batch sizes. we log tokens/sec, median/95 latency, GPU util, and an estimated cost per token based on observed throughput. we also tag runs with kernel selection like f8* kernels or aten kernels depending on hardware. sometimes public names change so the catalog keeps an internal kernel map.
[02:40] Jia: do you run with quantization knobs in the bench? we care about INT8 vs FP16 quality delta.
[02:45] Samir: yes — we surface quantization profiles; for each profile we have a small quality delta estimate from our eval suite, but customer-specific evals are recommended. the Optimize tab suggests a profile based on your workload mix — e.g., if embeddings/similarity-heavy, we may recommend 4-bit quant and batching aggressively.
[03:05] Alex: what about private deployments — can we have the control-plane managed by Redwood but inference in our VPC?
[03:11] Priya: yes, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane where the control plane is still visible in the console but the data path sits in your VPC. we integrate with your KMS for model encryption at rest and CMEK if needed. also audit logs stream to your SIEM.
[03:28] Daniel: ok what about SSO and RBAC? auditors will ask.
[03:33] Priya: SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning, role-based permissions, and we can provide an audit log export. SOC2+ISO artifacts are in the security pack I'll send.
[03:45] Alex: nice. on the bench — how do we run a side-by-side comparing Hosted and Dedicated — we want to understand p95 differences and costs.
[03:51] Samir: for that we propose a 2-week POC: we replay a subset of your production queries against three shortlisted models on both Hosted endpoints and a Dedicated pool configured to your latency SLO. we'll instrument token-level cost and latency and produce CSVs with per-query breakdowns.
[04:10] Alex: timelines? we can give sample data Monday.
[04:13] Priya: great, then Samir can kick off bench on Wednesday once we get infra creds or a static sample. we'll also ask for a small spike on your onprem box for one model to validate kernel compatibility.
[04:25] Jia: question — how deterministic is kernel mapping? we sometimes see different kernels chosen at first-token vs streaming tails.
[04:31] Samir: kernel selection is heuristic; it's deterministic given model binary, runtime version, and seq length distribution. there are edge cases with certain fused kernels where we fallback to a generic path which slightly increases latency — those are flagged in the compatibility matrix as 'fallback risk'.
[04:48] Alex: good to know. could you show the API path for programmatic model selection? we want to wire this into our feature flag system.
[04:53] Priya: yes — /v1/models returns the catalog with metadata fields like compat_kernels, quant_profiles, bench_summary — you can request a variant by model_id:variant. we also have an admin route to pin a model version for a customer tenancy to avoid accidental auto-rollouts.
[05:10] Daniel: is the console's canary routing manual or automatic? if a model starts failing we want auto-fallback to a fallback variant.
[05:16] Priya: both — you can define automatic fallback policies based on error rate or latency thresholds. you can also pair with traffic shaping to route X% to new variant as a canary.
[05:28] Alex: on cost — can you walk through a sample TCO estimate? we have 400 requests/sec, average reply 60 tokens.
[05:34] Samir: rough calc: tokens/sec = 400 * 60 = 24k tokens/sec, convert to hourly and multiply by cost per token per model variant — Optimize has a TCO calculator where you plug qps, seq len, desired p95 and it suggests batching and quant settings to hit a cost target. we'll run your numbers in the POC.
[05:55] Jia: send us an example calc exported to CSV, that would be helpful.
[05:58] Priya: yes, Samir will include a sample CSV with the bench template.
[06:02] Alex: any legal gotchas with open models — licensing?
[06:05] Priya: we annotate license info in the catalog and flag models with restrictive terms — you'll see license_type column. for any unusual restrictions we'll raise it with legal.
[06:16] Daniel: a couple quick nitty gritty: can we control KV cache TTL and evictions? we have a stateful chat app.
[06:23] Samir: yes TTLs and cache policies are configurable in Dedicated/Private runtime; Hosted supports some config but with platform defaults. cache metrics are exposed in the console.
[06:33] Alex: ok last thing — quality checks. we don't want hallucination regressions if we quantize aggressively.
[06:39] Samir: totally — part of the POC is a small quality eval set from you; we'll run model+quant combinations and report rubric scores. if a quantized profile causes unacceptable degradation we won't recommend it for that route.
[06:55] Priya: wrap-up — next steps: I'll send the security pack and SOC2 summary by Friday, Samir will upload the bench template and sample CSV, and we'll schedule the POC kickoff for Oct 12 pending your infra creds.
[07:10] Alex: sounds good. Jia will share the production traffic snapshot and the on-prem hardware specs.
[07:15] Jia: yes will do.
[07:17] Daniel: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[07:20] Priya: thank you all, we'll follow up in the thread with links.
[07:24] (end recording)

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription occasionally mangles technical terms (e.g., 'KV cache' -> 'K V cash', 'quantization' -> 'quant eight zation' in some spots). small amounts of crosstalk and filler removed for readability but most verbatim preserved.
